hook: Nearly a third of annual giving happens in December. Your year-end campaign starts now — not Thanksgiving week.
direction: Year-end giving timeline for ministries and nonprofits: October = plan and segment, November = warm the list with impact stories, December = the ask series. Timeline graphic.

facebook.text:
Nearly a third of annual giving happens in December. Your year-end campaign starts now — not Thanksgiving week.

Here's the timeline that works:

October: Plan your campaign and segment your donor list. Who gave last year? Who lapsed? Who's new?

November: Warm the list. Share impact stories. Let donors see what their giving actually did.

December: Make the ask — clearly, more than once, without apology.

Most ministries and nonprofits wait too long and then rush the ask. The ones that plan in October show up in December with credibility already built. Start now.

instagram.text:
Nearly a third of annual giving happens in December.

That means your year-end campaign starts in October — not the week before Thanksgiving.

Here's the three-month timeline:

October → Plan and segment your donor list
November → Warm the list with real impact stories
December → The ask series

The ministries and nonprofits that do this well aren't more talented. They just started earlier. Save this and get moving.
